intro.text: A Scadrian power at war with Roshar, eager to claim the perpendicularity it believes lies hidden in the Drominad system.
A nation on Scadrial that dominates its home world and ranks among the strongest powers in the cosmere. Many regard it as an aggressive, fascist regime.

description.text: The Malwish build great numbers of civilian and military spacecraft entirely by themselves, from large capital ships that serve as bases when meeting new peoples to sleek, silvery triangular landers that seem to fly by Steelpushing. Like most ships in the cosmere, theirs burn aethers, mostly mined on distant Lumar, and Scadrians earn a fortune selling parts such as hulls. They claim, and truly believe, that theirs is the cosmere's most advanced world, though many disagree.

Beyond Scadrial, the Malwish rule all or part of several planets, some independent in name only, each under a colonial governor who may be a native. Scadrians own the best property in these dominions and draw their riches home. The Malwish habitually claim land, send patrols and write their own rules: they police about half the Shadesmar lanes between worlds, though not near Silverlight, and can declare places under their "exploratory jurisdiction".

Their military, probably among the richest in the cosmere, is known for aggression and strict discipline. It fields capital ships whose guns can flatten a city with a shot or two, smaller capital ships and highly rated fighters, all working best inside a Scadrian steelfield. It keeps installations across the cosmere, where trespassers can be jailed and their property seized, and pays pensions to the spouses of the fallen.

Many Malwish wear masks, though they often take them off, putting them back on to concentrate or when things turn serious. Some are pairs of small metal grafts fixed to the skin along the cheekbones; others are tiny metal pieces at the edges of the face. Full arcanists may wear ceremonial masks of carved wood painted black, and soldiers may don angular war masks plating the forehead, cheeks and nose, which many find intimidating.

items.text: The Malwish fight at least some of Roshar's powers, though no side dares a full invasion. Instead they jostle for territory and advantage, fight the odd battle or skirmish, and try to intimidate everyone else. Both sides are competing to claim Drominad.

During the war it became clear that a planet in the Drominad system, which Scadrians call Drominad, held great Investiture. Old reports of its gifted birds pointed to a hidden perpendicularity, worth even more than the birds: it would open a new region to cheap travel, saving fortunes on FTL, and strengthen the Malwish, since the planet lies between Roshar and Scadrial.

The Malwish reached the planet and contacted the Eelakin, who were just entering their industrial age and knew nothing of the wider cosmere. Wary of angering a Shard, they could not simply invade and had to win the world by treaty. They offered new technology and tried to buy the birds, but the Eelakin refused to sell; meanwhile the Malwish hunted for the perpendicularity, once even asking the Eelakin outright.

To the Eelakin they were the Ones Above, godlike beings with wondrous technology, drawn in the broadsheets of the day with dark holes for faces. Treaties allowed an invasion only if the Eelakin posed a threat.

As years passed with neither the perpendicularity nor a deal for the birds, the Malwish grew impatient. They pushed new technology on the Eelakin to create a lawful excuse for conquest, made the islands rely on their goods and held back shipments until life there stalled, and after eight years had the Eelakin cornered.

Meanwhile, in the Cognitive Realm, they found a small ring-shaped island around a moat, its inner island guarded by a giant Invested snake and reached by a deadly tunnel. Colonel Dajer's force believed the perpendicularity lay beyond, but everyone and every machine sent through the tunnel was lost, and the snake stopped anything from flying across.

In those years starfighters grew far more costly, and the Malwish secretly built a new device, the Intensifier, letting a few outside arcanists see its power. With it they broke the lock on a dragon ancestral cavern. Six years after first contact with the Eelakin, partisans assassinated Prime Minister Yadramak while he met a Sleepless spy; some of the spy's nodes died too, so the Malwish blamed the Sleepless.

After three weeks stuck at the tunnel, Dajer's men seized a trading ship and a native who had rowed up to the island. He got through the tunnel, found it led nowhere, then crossed to the inner island and bound the snake, the Dakwara, which killed Dajer as the traders fled. He led it to the true perpendicularity, which it now guards, and the Malwish had to quit the planet and give up hope of ruling it.
